channel.title: Smithsonian / USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report
channel.description: The Weekly Volcanic Activity Report is a cooperative project between the Smithsonian's Global Volcanism Program and the US Geological Survey's Volcano Hazards Program. Updated by 2300 UTC every Thursday, these notices are preliminary and subject to change as events are studied in more detail. This is not a comprehensive list of eruptions during the week, but rather a summary of activity that meet selected criteria. Carefully reviewed, detailed reports are published in the Bulletin of the Global Volcanism Network.

item.title: Ambae (Vanuatu) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Vanuatu Meteorology and Geohazards Department (VMGD) reported that the eruption at Ambae continued during 21-26 August, with explosive activity producing tall ash plumes on 25 August. Continuous plumes of gas, steam, and ash were visible in satellite and webcam images drifting NW during 21-24 August and drifting NE on 25 August. Sulfur dioxide gas emissions were at moderate to high levels, and seismicity indicated high levels of activity. Thermal anomalies were identified in satellite data. The Wellington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC) reported that ash plumes were significantly higher during 25-26 August. The eruption escalated at 2040 on 25 August, and by 2124 an ash plume had risen to 16.5 km (54,000 ft) a.s.l. and was drifting E based on satellite images. The ash plume altitude decreased to 15.2 km (50,000 ft) a.s.l. by 2153 and to 12.8 km (42,000 ft) a.s.l. by 0013 on 26 August. A strong sulfur dioxide signal was also detected. Ash plumes continued to be detected during the rest of the day on 26 August rising 3-4.6 km (10,000-15,000 ft) a.s.l. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 0-5), and the public was warned to stay outside of Danger Zone B, defined as a 3-km radius around the active vents in Lake Voui, and to stay away from drainages during heavy rains.

Sources: Vanuatu Meteorology and Geohazards Department (VMGD),Wellington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC)

item.title: Karangetang (Indonesia) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) and a news source reported that an eruption at Karangetang?s North Crater (Kawah Dua) continued during 20-26 August. Daily white plumes rose as high as 400 m above the summit and drifted in various directions. Incandescence at both the North and South craters was visible in some webcam images throughout the week, but was stronger at North Crater. Seismicity was variable but at high levels, and rumbling sounds were occasionally heard. Incandescence at the North summit and from the lava flows on the flanks was visible in webcam images at 0019 on 26 August and at 0737 on 27 August. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was advised to stay 1.5 km away from both craters, with an extension to 2.5 km on the NW and SW flanks of North Crater.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Klyuchevskoy (Russia) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported that the eruption at Klyuchevskoy continued at the summit crater during 20-26 August. A thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images on most days; weather clouds sometimes obscured views. Ash plumes periodically rose as high as 6 km (19,680 ft) a.s.l. and drifted as far as 500 km NE and E. The Aviation Color Code remained at Orange (the second highest level on a four-color scale). Dates are based on UTC; specific events are in local time where noted.

Source: Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT)

item.title: Krakatau (Indonesia) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Krakatau during 20-26 August. Daily ash-and-gas plumes that were a mixture of white, gray, and black colors rose 100-400 m above the summit and drifted mainly NW, W, and SW. Several webcam images showed incandescent material being ejected above the crater. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was advised to stay 3 km away from summit.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Villarrica (Chile) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:

item.title: Aira (Japan) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Minamidake Crater (Aira Caldera?s Sakurajima volcano) during 17-24 August. Crater incandescence was visible in nighttime webcam images. An eruptive event at 2029 on 17 August generated an ash plume that rose as high as 1.9 km above the summit. An ash plume from an explosion at 0538 on 19 August rose as high as 1.3 km above the summit and drifted NW. Very small eruptive events were recorded during 21-24 August. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a 5-level scale), and the public was warned to be cautious within 1 km of both the Minimadake and Showa craters.

Source: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA)

item.title: Dukono (Indonesia) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that eruptive activity at Dukono continued during 20-26 August. White-and-gray ash plumes rose as high as 1.4 km above the summit and drifted in various directions on most days; weather conditions obscured views on 26 August. The Alert Level remained at Level 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay 4 km away from the Malupang Warirang Crater.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Etna (Italy) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV) reported eruptive activity at Etna?s summit craters during 17-23 August characterized by weak explosive activity and ash emissions at Voragine Crater (VOR), Bocca Nuova (BN) Crater, and Northeast Crater (NEC), and effusive activity from two vents within the Valle del Bove. Weak and intermittent explosive activity at VOR persisted during most of the week with diffuse ash emissions dissipating around the summit. Diffuse, ongoing emissions at BN and NEC craters were recorded by webcams. Lava effusion continued from the vent at 1,900 m elevation during most of the week. Active and overlapping flows did not extend below 1,500 m elevation. The Aviation Color Code (ACC) was lowered to Orange (the second highest color on a four-color scale) on 18 August because explosive activity was decreasing. A new vent opened at 3,060 m elevation on 18 August, produced a 600-m-long lava flow, and was inactive by 19 August. Lava was no longer flowing from VOR into NEC by 19 August. The leading lava flow had reached an elevation of 1,315 m in the vicinity of Rocca Musarra by 19 August, but by 23 August the vent at 1,900 m elevation was no longer active. The ACC was lowered to Yellow on 24 August and to Green on 26 August. The volcano Alert Level remained at Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) according to the Dipartimento della Protezione Civile.

Sources: Dipartimento della Protezione Civile,Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV)

item.title: Fuego (Guatemala) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Instituto Nacional de Sismolog�a, Vulcanologia, Meteorologia e Hidrolog�a (INSIVUMEH) reported that eruptive activity at Fuego continued during 19-26 August. Daily explosions recorded by the seismic network, at rates of 2-10 per hour when reported, generated gas-and-ash plumes that rose as high as 1.1 km above the summit and drifted as far as 60 km SW, W, and NW. Explosions produced shock waves and rumbling or jet engine sounds that were reported daily and sometimes caused roofs and structures to vibrate. Explosions occasionally ejected incandescent material as high as 400 m above the summit and onto the flanks, causing incandescent block avalanches; notably avalanches descended the Seca (W), Taniluy� (SSW), Ceniza (SSW), Trinidad (SSW), and Las Lajas (SE) drainages, sometimes reaching vegetated areas. Ash fell in areas on the W flank during 19-20 August. Ashfall was reported in Sangre de Cristo (8 km W), San Pedro Yepocapa (8 km NW), Pochuta, and surrounding areas during 20-21 August, in San Pedro Yepocapa during 22-24 August and in Panimach� (8 km SW), Morelia (10 km SW), Santa Sofia (12 km SW), El Porvenir (11 km SW), San Pedro Yepocapa, Sangre de Cristo, and other nearby communities during 23-24 August.

Source: Instituto Nacional de Sismologia, Vulcanologia, Meteorologia, e Hidrologia (INSIVUMEH)

item.title: Great Sitkin (United States) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Alaska Volcano Observatory (AVO) reported that slow lava effusion continued to feed a thick flow in Great Sitkin?s summit crater during 19-26 August based on webcam and satellite images. The flow gradually expanded E. Minor earthquakes were detected daily, likely associated with rockfalls on the growing dome. Slightly elevated surface temperatures were identified in satellite images during 24-25 August. Weather clouds often obscured webcam and satellite views during most of the week. The Volcano Alert Level remained at Watch (the third level on a four-level scale) and the Aviation Color Code remained at Orange (the third color on a four-color scale).

Source: US Geological Survey Alaska Volcano Observatory (AVO)

item.title: Ibu (Indonesia) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity at Ibu continued during 20-26 August, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. Gray or white-to-gray ash plumes rose 300-1,000 m above the summit and drifted in multiple directions, especially towards the N, NE, and SE. Incandescence at the summit was visible in some nighttime webcam images. The Alert Level remained at 2 (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) and the public was advised to stay 2 km away from the active crater and 3.5 km away from the N crater wall opening.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Kanlaon (Philippines) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported continuing eruptive activity at Kanlaon during 19-26 August. The seismic network recorded 0-8 daily volcanic earthquakes; the counts included three periods of tremor during 24-25 August, lasting 21 minutes to five hours and 42 minutes. Sulfur dioxide emissions ranged from 1,244 to 2,092 tonnes per day. Volcanic emissions rose as high as 300 m above the summit and drifted NNE, ENE, and E on most days; observations were obscured on 19 August. Ash emissions were periodically recorded during the week. At 0524 on 20 August a grayish ash emission rose 200 m above the crater rim and drifted E. A total of five ash emissions were recorded on 22 August, each lasting 17 minutes to nearly five hours. At least two of the plumes, at 1123 and 1511, were voluminous, rose 150 m above the crater rim, and drifted SE. The webcam recorded hot emissions during 2305-2359. Two grayish ash emissions on 23 August lasted 33 minutes and nearly two hours, rose 150 m above the crater rim, and drifted SE. On 24 August there were three ash emissions, each lasting 23 minutes to six hours. One of the ash plumes rose 200 m above the crater rim and drifted E at 0551. A grayish ash emission lasted for 30 seconds and drifted ENE on 25 August. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 0-5); the public was warned to stay out of the 4-km-radius Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ) and pilots were advised to avoid flying close to the summit.

Source: Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS)

item.title: Kilauea (United States) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO) reported that the eruption within Kilauea?s Kaluapele summit caldera, characterized by episodic fountaining, incandescence, and intermittent spatter from craters along the SW margin of Halema`uma`u Crater, continued at variable levels during 19-26 August. Continuous moderate to strong incandescence at the N vent was observed along with weak and intermittent incandescence at the W vent during most of the week. The S vent appeared dark. Weak spattering at the N vent began at around 1930 on 24 August and became continuous at around midnight. Bright glow, flames, and occasional spatter were observed from the W vent and correlated with tremor peaks produced by lava drainbacks during gas-piston cycles. Lava overflowed the N vent and a small dome fountain was active during 0616-0637 on 25 August. In response, HVO raised the Volcano Alert Level to Watch (the second highest level on a four-level scale) and the Aviation Color Code to Orange (the second highest color on a four-color scale) at 0638. Lava overflowed the vent during 0727-0812. Continuous low-level fountaining began at around 0900 and lava overflows continued through 1003. The lava fountain grew in height and volume at 1030 and by 1043 the fountain was at most 20 m high. Lava flowed onto the crater floor. The fountain grew rapidly, reaching a sustained peak height of 150 m during 1215-1300. The lava fountain produced significant heat and some tephra, creating an eruption plume that rose as high as 5.2 km (17,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifted SW based on webcam images. By 1330 the fountain decreased in height to 110 m and remained at that level until 1800. The eruption plume decreased to 4.2 km (14,000 ft) a.s.l. by 1330 and continued to decrease through the afternoon. Tephra mainly fell within the closed area of Hawai`i Volcanoes National Park, SW of the active eruptive vents in Halema`uma`u, though trace amounts of Pele?s hair fell in the Ka`u district. The fountain height was 50 m tall by 1900 and fluctuated between 30 and 60 m during the last 30 minutes; the episode ended at 1933, after 9 hours of continuous fountaining. The last 3 minutes were marked by gas jetting and flaming at the same vent. The average effusion rate was 110 cubic meters per second; the highest peak was 220 cubic meters per second, occurring at around 1145. An estimated 5.2 million cubic meters of lava erupted and covered 30 percent of the Halema`uma`u Crater floor. At 1947 the Volcano Alert Level was lowered to Advisory and the Aviation Color Code was lowered to Yellow.

Source: US Geological Survey Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO)

item.title: Langila (Papua New Guinea) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Darwin Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre (VAAC) reported that an ash plume from Langila rose 1.8 km (6,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifted NW on 24 August based on satellite images. On 26 August an ash plume rose 2.1 km (7,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifted NW.

Source: Darwin Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre (VAAC)

item.title: Lewotobi (Indonesia) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that eruptive activity continued at Lewotobi Laki-Laki during 20-26 August. Multiple daily gray ash plumes rose 200-1,000 m above the summit and drifted mainly NW, W, and SW on most days; white plumes rose as high as 100 m above the summit on 26 August. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 1-4), and the public was warned to stay 5 km away from the center of Laki-Laki.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Lewotolok (Indonesia) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported continuing eruptive activity at Lewotolok during 20-26 August. Daily white plumes rose as high as 300 m above the summit and drifted NW, W, and SW. Incandescent material was ejected above the summit and onto the flanks. Active lava flows were 1.2 km long on the S flank and about 500 m long on the NE flank by 20 August; the flows were incandescent in a 21 August webcam image. At 2023 on 24 August a white-and-gray ash plume rose 400 m above the summit and drifted W. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4). The public was warned to stay 2 km away from the summit with an extension to 3 km on the S and SE flanks.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Popocatepetl (Mexico) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:

The seismic network recorded 4-13 long-period events per day, accompanied by steam-and-gas emissions; the emissions contained ash that drifted NE, NW, and W during 22-25 August. Source: Centro Nacional de Prevencion de Desastres (CENAPRED)

item.title: Purace (Colombia) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Servicio Geologico Colombiano (SGC) reported intensifying eruptive activity at Purac� during 18-26 August. Signals associated with fluid movement dominated the seismicity and were characterized as tremor-type signals and, to a lesser extent, long-period events located beneath Purac� volcano at depths less than 2 km. Seismic activity associated with rock fracturing was low in both number and magnitude, with signals located at depths less than 5 km. Sulfur dioxide flux stayed above the average baseline level, averaging 3,230 tonnes per day (t/d) on 20 August and 1,300 t/d on 26 August. Soil carbon dioxide concentrations rose throughout the reporting period. Slow ground deformation persisted in an area between the Purac�, Piocollo, and Curiquinga volcanoes. A few daily ash emissions were recorded by the seismic network and visible in webcam images when not obscured by weather clouds. The ash plumes rose as high as 2.6 km above the summit and caused ashfall in areas downwind on most days. Ashfall was reported in the villages of Cristales, Loma Linda, and Alto de Anamb�o during 18-19 August, in Paletar� (16 km SW), La Josefina (15 km SW), El Dep�sito, Jigual, Loma Linda, Cristales, Alto de Anamb�o (7 km NW), El Crucero, Campamento, La Palma, Tabio, Chap�o Alto (9 km NW), Hispala (32 km NW), Hato Viejo (12 km WNW), 20 de Julio, and Pulul� during 19-20 August, in Cristales and Hispala (32 km NW) during 20-21 August, and in Cobal� (11 km W), 20 de Julio, Hato Viejo, Ambir�, and Patico (12 km NW) during 22-23 August. Residents also reported a strong sulfur odor during 19-20 August. An ash plume that rose to 2.6 km above the summit at 1258 on 25 August was associated with loud noises heard by residents of Cristales. The Alert Level remained at Orange (the second highest level on a four-color scale).

Source: Servicio Geol�gico Colombiano (SGC)

item.title: Rincon de la Vieja (Costa Rica) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Observatorio Vulcanol�gico y Sismol�gico de Costa Rica-Universidad Nacional (OVSICORI-UNA) reported that one or two small phreatic eruptions per day at Rinc�n de la Vieja were recorded by the seismic and infrasound networks during 20-23 and 25 August. None of the events were visually observed. An eruptive event at 1413 on 24 August generated a voluminous plume that rose 1. 5 km above the crater rim and drifted SW. The Alert Level remained at 3 (Caution) and the Aviation Color Code remained Orange.

Source: Observatorio Vulcanologico y Sismologico de Costa Rica-Universidad Nacional (OVSICORI-UNA)

item.title: Sabancaya (Peru) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Instituto Geof�sico del Per�?s (IGP) Centro Vulcanol�gico Nacional (CENVUL) reported continuing eruptive activity at Sabancaya during 17-23 August. The seismic network detected 34 seismic events associated with the movement of magmatic fluids, along with earthquakes indicating internal rock fracturing; no volcanic explosions occurred during the period. Gas, steam, and ash emissions periodically rose as high as 800 m above the summit and drifted less than 10 km E and SE. Moderate sulfur dioxide (SO?) emissions averaged 879 tons per day, and four thermal anomalies (each 4 MW or less) associated with the lava dome were identified. The Alert Level remained at Orange (the third level on a four-color scale) and the public was warned to stay outside of a 12 km radius from the summit.

Source: Instituto Geof�sico del Per� (IGP)

item.title: Santa Maria (Guatemala) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Instituto Nacional de Sismolog�a, Vulcanolog�a, Meteorolog�a e Hidrolog�a (INSIVUMEH) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Santa Maria?s Santiaguito dome complex during 19-26 August, with continuing lava extrusion at Caliente dome. Incandescence at the summit was observed during dark hours. Effusion of blocky lava and collapses of material produced daily incandescent block avalanches that descended the flanks; during 20-21 and 23-24 August these collapses generated short pyroclastic flows that reached the base on the cone. Daily explosions, 1-4 per hour when reported, generated gas-and-ash plumes that rose 700-800 m above the dome and drifted SW and W. Ashfall was reported in Loma Linda (7 km W), San Marcos Palajunoj, and other nearby communities during 20-21 and 23-24 August, and in Finca Powilonia, Rosario, San Marcos Palajunoj (10 km SW), Bohemia (9 km SW), La Tranquilidad (7 km SW), Nueva Delfina (8 km SW), Helvetia (10 km SW), and La Suiza during 22-23 August.

Source: Instituto Nacional de Sismologia, Vulcanologia, Meteorologia, e Hidrologia (INSIVUMEH)

item.title: Semeru (Indonesia) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity continued at Semeru during 20-26 August, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. Daily white-to-gray or gray ash plumes rose 400-1,100 m above the summit and drifted multiple directions. A few webcam images showed incandescence at the summit and incandescent material on the upper SE flank. The Alert Level remained at 3 (the second highest level on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay at least 5 km away from the Jonggring Saloko Crater in all directions, 13 km from the summit on the SE flank along the Kobokan drainage, and 500 m from the banks of the Kobokan drainage as far as 17 km SE of the summit.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Sheveluch (Russia) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported continuing lava effusion and explosive activity at the lava domes along the N crater floor of Young Sheveluch (on the SW flank of Old Sheveluch) during 19-26 August. A thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images on most days; weather clouds occasionally obscured views. The Aviation Color Code remained at Orange (the second highest level on a four-color scale). Dates are based on UTC; specific events are in local time where noted.

Source: Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT)

item.title: Stromboli (Italy) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV) reported that eruptive activity continued at Stromboli during 17-23 August. Webcam images showed Strombolian activity from vents in Area N within the upper part of the Sciara del Fuoco, and vents in Area C-S (South-Central Crater) on the crater terrace. The vents in Area N produced medium- to high-intensity explosions that ejected lapilli and bombs above the vents. Explosions at vents in Area C-S were low-to-moderate in intensity and frequency, which ejected both fine and coarse tephra above the vents. The Alert Level remained at Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) according to the Dipartimento della Protezione Civile.

Sources: Dipartimento della Protezione Civile,Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV)

item.title: Telica (Nicaragua) - Report for 20 August-26 August 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC) reported that an ash plume at Telica was identified in webcam and satellite images on 20 August rising to 1.2 km (4,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifting SW.

Source: Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC)
